In deep learning, the positional encoding or position embedding is a component of sequence models, especially Transformers. Input data such as text, images, or audio is converted to a sequence of numerical representations called tokens, and the position of each token is encoded as a vector. Positional encoding is used because the standard attention mechanism used in Transformers by default treats all tokens symmetrically over all positions (i.e. permutation-symmetric), thus effectively treating the input as a bag of tokens, rather than a sequence of tokens.
